A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, and their text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison. v1 ends after the references; v2 adds readable Appendices A–E.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments on five datasets, mitigation experiments, confusion matrices, and tokenization and attention analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds open-source few-shot results, explicit-prompt comparisons, and a human classification study.

M1.justification: The word-selection and vertical-transformation algorithm in Section 3 and the proposed three-shot mitigation with manually constructed analyses remain unchanged. Appendix D evaluates an additional prompting comparator without revising these procedures.

E1.justification: The same five datasets and classification tasks remain. Appendix E adds a human-study population of three graduate students who are native English speakers, evaluated on four retained datasets. The mathematical and Sudoku examples added to the abstract are not evaluated tasks.

E2.justification: Appendix D adds explicit reconstruction instructions as a comparator to naive and three-shot prompting for GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 on SST-2 and Rotten Tomatoes. Appendix E adds human reference performance. Existing comparisons remain available.

E3.justification: v2 adds a distinct human evaluation design: participants classify both original and vertical inputs, with texts reshuffled between presentations. It also introduces explicit-prompt conditions and extends three-shot evaluation to Llama3.1-8B and Gemma2-9B. Section 6.1 changes the tokenizer example's reported model from Llama3-8B to Llama3.1-8B, without establishing a rerun. The main balanced 100-sample evaluations and accuracy metric remain.

E4.justification: Appendix D newly tests whether explicit instructions to recognize and reconstruct vertical words suffice to mitigate the vulnerability. Appendix E directly tests human sensitivity to the same formatting manipulation. These add substantive control and robustness analyses; the original word-count sensitivity, confusion matrices, and attention analyses remain.

E5.justification: Appendix E and Table 5 newly report averaging accuracy across three human evaluations. No participant variability, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests accompany these averages, and no additional LLM run counts or seeds are disclosed.

E6.justification: Original table and figure results remain unchanged. Figure 9 adds three-shot gains of 18–19 percentage points for Llama3.1-8B and 14–15 for Gemma2-9B; Appendix C reverses these attributions. Figure 10 adds explicit-prompt gains of 2–9 points, and Table 5 reports nearly unchanged human accuracy across formats. The new claim of larger Llama3.1-8B drops on four datasets conflicts with Table 1's raw scores: Rotten Tomatoes drops are 35 versus 44 points for Llama3-8B.

T1.justification: The accuracy equation in Section 4.3 is unchanged. Neither version supplies formal theoretical results or proofs, and the tokenization and attention discussions remain empirical and conceptual.

C1.justification: The abstract's findings, introduction's contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims: vertical formatting harms classification, CoT offers little mitigation, analyzed few-shot examples help, and tokenization and attention explain the vulnerability. The revised abstract opening changes motivation without redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix D adds a practical limitation: explicit format-aware prompts have restricted applicability when models face many different vulnerabilities. Appendix E attributes tiny human accuracy differences to randomness, and Appendix C relates mitigation differences to model capabilities. The original mechanism explanations and dedicated Limitations section remain.

D1.justification: Most implementation information moves from Section 4.4 to Appendix B unchanged. However, open-source inference is now described as using Hugging Face weights or official APIs instead of llama-api and Groq. Section 6.1 removes token ID 15651, and Figure 11 supplies the explicit sentiment-classification prompt.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to prior vertical-text attacks and prompt-sensitivity research remain unchanged. The Radford et al. reference receives bibliographic metadata updates, not a substantive citation or positioning change.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the abstract opening, makes local explanatory edits, moves implementation details into Appendix B, and adds Appendices A–E, including model descriptions. The main narrative and section sequence are largely retained.

P2.justification: Tables 1 and 4 are respaced and recolored; Table 4 now distinguishes increases in green, decreases in red, and ties in black. v2 adds Figures 9–11 and Table 5. Figure 10 redisplays some existing scores alongside new explicit-prompt results. Existing figures and the overall layout remain largely intact.

improvement.justification: Appendices C–E strengthen the evidence by testing v1's human-readability premise, adding an explicit-prompt control, and extending few-shot evaluation beyond GPT models. The displayed results support these additions, but the gain is limited by the three-person human study without uncertainty estimates and new reporting inconsistencies: Appendix C reverses the models' gains, and the four-dataset Llama comparison conflicts with Table 1's raw accuracies.
